newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS USE 55 SHOTS TO BEAT PHOENIX.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS USE 55 SHOTS TO BEAT PHOENIX.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers peppered Phoenix goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin with a season-high 55 shots, and salted away a 4-1 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes Tuesday.
"When you get 55 shots, you're bound to get a few in," said Philadelphia star Eric Lindros. "It it wasn't for their goaltending at the other end, it would've been a bit of a blowout."
Shjon Podein scored twice for the Flyers, snapping a 15-game goal-scoring drought.
"I don't think there's any secret after 15 games, but it was nice to break out and help the team with a couple of points," Podein said, commenting on scoring the Flyers' first goal.
"We needed those two points. When it went in, I felt a heavy thing lift off my chest, a lot of guilt, it really felt good."

"You just keep plugging away, putting the puck to the net and Pods (Podein) got himself into good position a couple of times," Philadelphia coach Terry Murray said. "It was good to see him break out of it and he had a real solid game."

Lindros and Janne Niinimaa also tallied for Philadelphia, which snapped a three-game winless streak and maintained its three-point lead over second-place Florida in the Atlantic Division. Phoenix has lost four of six.
Khabibulin tied a career-high with his 51 saves. He also made 51 at Detroit in Game 5 of the Western Conference quarterfinals last April 26.
Garth Snow stopped 17 shots to extend his personal unbeaten streak to eight games.

Snow held Phoenix scoreless over the first two periods, stopping all 11 shots he faced, before Bob Corkum's goal with 3:56 remaining spoiled the shutout. Snow improved to 5-0-3 in his last eight decisions.
"We got dominated by a hard-working hockey team," Phoenix coach Don Hay said. "They were very physical and they just outworked us.
"We didn't push back. If it wasn't for Nick ... he's keeping us in the game, he was the one guy who really came to play tonight."

"We didn't want to play physical, we just wanted to watch them skate around," Coyotes centre Jeremy Roenick said. "They're a big team and we watched them. We were spectators tonight, plain and simple."
At Florida, John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 30 shots and Scott Mellanby had a pair of goals and an assist as the Panthers routed the reeling Montreal Canadiens 5-1.
Vanbiesbrouck held the Canadiens in check over the first 35 minutes in improving to 17-10-7.

"We feel confident in our defence, which is the whole focal point of winning," Vanbiesbrouck said. "You can talk about scoring goals all you want, but real hard work and where it's at is in our own end. Then the goals come naturally."
Mellanby, who has four goals in his last two games, has 20 on the season. He is tied for the team lead with Ray Sheppard, who scored his 20th midway through the second period.

"I've been a lot more patient lately," Mellanby said. "The coaches have pointed out I should be staying higher in the slot. All my career I've gone to the net., I'm getting used to this now. I don't want to say that I've found all the answers, but on both my goals there was nobody in front of me."
Robert Svehla and Rob Niedermayer added two assists apiece for the Panthers, who have won three straight and have taken two of three meetings from the Canadiens this season.
Chris Murray had the lone goal for Montreal, which has dropped four straight and has been outscored 24-5 over that span.
In Calgary, Steve Chiasson and Mike Sullivan scored shorthanded goals and Aaron Gavey added a goal and an assist as the Flames held on for a 4-3 victory over the New York Islanders.
Corey Millen also tallied for the Calgary, which snapped a three-game winless streak. The Flames have won four of their last five at home, where they improved to 11-10-2.
Calgary carried a 4-1 lead into the third period, but Bryan Smolinski scored twice to cut the margin to one goal.
